diff: So the German book year opens every spring in Leipzig and peaks every autumn in Frankfurt. Even in the GDR era the Leipzig fair kept a window open: from 1952 Western publishers were represented there again, and for decades it was one of the few places where readers and publishers from East and West could meet.

So beginnt das deutsche Bücherjahr jedes Frühjahr in Leipzig und erreicht jeden Herbst in Frankfurt seinen Höhepunkt. Selbst zu DDR-Zeiten hielt die Leipziger Messe ein Fenster offen: Ab 1952 waren dort wieder westliche Verlage vertreten, und jahrzehntelang war sie einer der wenigen Orte, an denen sich Leser und Verlage aus Ost und West begegnen konnten.

entries.reason: a1382 body: Frankfurt Book Fair "more than 7,000 exhibitors from over 100 countries" → "more than 4,000 exhibitors from over 90 countries" — outdated (2025: 4,350 from 93) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt_Book_Fair
a1382 body: Büchner Prize winners list "Herta Müller" → "Christa Wolf" — Müller never won the Büchner Prize (Wolf 1980) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_B%C3%BCchner_Prize

a1382 body: "Bologna Ragazzi Awards for illustration" → "BolognaRagazzi Awards for outstanding children's books" — the awards are for books (fiction, non-fiction …), illustration has its own exhibition — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bologna_Children%27s_Book_Fair
a1382: Bologna's first fair "April 1964 in the Palazzo Re Enzo" confirmed by Publishers Weekly, while English Wikipedia says the fair has run "since 1963" (1963 was the planning year).
